text.p: Monday's sharp jump in shares of Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc, after their surprise 24 billion stg merger, was icing on the cake for investors who have already enjoyed a sharp recovery in both stocks this year.

From year's lows set the same day -- January 17, when LVMH Moet Hennessey Louis Vuitton sold a third of its stake in Guinness to the UK group -- Guinness had already risen 30 percent by Friday's close while Grand Met was up 24 percent, according to Reuters Securities 3000 data.
By comparison the FTSE 100 index, which on Friday set the latest of a series of record closing highs, had risen just ten percent through the same period.
Guinness was up 95p at 611-1/2 by 1127 GMT and Grand Met was up 92p at 607.
Yet their recent recovery, driven in part by signs of a recovery in global spirits markets, stands in stark contrast with a lacklustre performance by both stocks in previous months.
Over the past 12 months, Guinness underperformed the FTSE 100 by 13 percent, while Grand Met underperformed the benchmark UK index by seven percent, according to Securities 3000.

For months, both stocks were weighed down by worries of global pressure on spirits prices, partly dispelled by Guinness's comments at its 1996 results in March that it had seen the start of a turnaround for the first time since the early 1980s.

Securities 3000 also showed that the combined group would rank as the eighth largest UK company at current prices, with a market capitalisation of more than 24 billion stg -- putting it above banking group Barclays Plc, which ranked ninth with a market value of around 19 billion stg.
